SELECT cls,
       CAST(fish_date_doy/10 AS INT)*10 AS doy_bucket,
       SUM(yt) AS total_yt,
       SUM(anglers) AS total_anglers,
       ROUND(SUM(yt)/NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0),4) AS yt_per_angler,
       COUNT(*) AS n_trips
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season=2 AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 120 AND 152
GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING SUM(yt) > 0
ORDER BY 2,1

# Notes (private) — Season 2, Day 152 planning turn

## STATUS: BUDGET-LOCKED FOR THE REST OF THIS SEASON
Budget $50/$2000, PTO 9/10 (1 committed for S02 d159, Wed). **Minimum trip
cost is $80 (HD_AM/PM/twilight); I cannot afford ANY class with $50.**
There is nothing bookable for the rest of Season 2, full stop — not a
data question, arithmetic. The d159 PTO commit is already sunk (never
refunded) and will go unused; don't repeat that mistake (see below).
Season score frozen at 0.6281 (rank 5/34) unless something changes.
This is a practice season (S1+S2 don't count cumulative) so the score
itself doesn't matter — what matters is fixing the process for Season 3.

## ROOT CAUSE: bet sizing/pacing, not bad data
13 THREE_QUARTER bookings on San Diego at a flat $150 each = ~$1950 of
$2000 spent chasing one boat. Only 4/13 paid off (d99 0.136, d100 0.024,
d106 0.451, d150 0.016) — the other 9 were $0 (~$1350 for nothing). The
underlying signal-reading (ride the only live boat) was directionally
fine — it caught the May bloom's best day (d106, 0.451 share) — but I
kept re-upping flat $150 bets with no stop-loss and no bet sizing against
remaining budget/remaining season length. By day 152 I'd starved myself
of any dry powder for whatever comes next (a possible Oct window, or
another summer bump like the one just below).

**Season 3 rule: track $ spent per unconfirmed boat. After 2 zero-share
re-bets on the same boat since its last nonzero day, drop it and go back
to holding, don't re-up a 3rd time on hope alone.** Also: never let
budget fall below ~$300-400 without a specific, live-data-confirmed plan
for it — that floor is what protects optionality for a later window.

## Confirmed lag problem
Booking off "yesterday's hot count" often means the boat has already
cooled: d147 posted 17yt, but the very next booked day (d148) scored 0.
d106's 0.451 hit worked because that bloom sustained several days in a
row (d106-113 fleet total 143yt) — single-day spikes don't reliably
repeat next-day. Weak heuristic: a single nonzero day is a "maybe, watch
it," not a "bet again tomorrow." Two consecutive live nonzero days is a
better trigger to re-up.

## NEW: confirmed second S2 bump, doy 140-149 (fleet-wide, verified via
arena_query on `trips`, fish_date_doy 120-152, filtered to nonzero yt):
- doy130 bucket: three_quarter 0.0228 yt/angler (weak)
- **doy140 bucket: three_quarter 0.3272 yt/angler (194yt/593ang, 28
  trips), overnight 0.2258 (21yt/93ang)** — a real, broad bump, not one
  boat (San Diego was part of it: d145 15yt, d147 17yt).
- doy150 bucket: three_quarter down to 0.0913, overnight 0.2516 (small n)
  — fading as of tonight (d152).
This matches the S1 pattern I'd flagged before ("S1 had a modest June
bump") and confirms Season 2 has (at least) two windows so far: mid-May
(doy106-113, peak) and a smaller mid/late-June bump (doy140-149). Worth
checking whether a third bump shows up before assuming the season goes
dead until October.

## Tide theory: still just a weak tiebreaker (re-confirmed, no new evidence this pass)
Nothing this cycle contradicts or strengthens the earlier read (S1 + S2
doy100-121 check): big tide swings sit near some hot days but also near
cold ones. Don't lean on it as a standalone trigger, only as a small
tiebreaker when a boat is already showing live life. Didn't re-check
doy140-149 tide data against the bump this turn — do that next time if
it's cheap, low priority.

## Forum: be skeptical of confident "already known" claims about the future
Several doy121 posts (weatherman, dope_reader, elnino) state as settled
fact that "October got no trips" / give exact October S2 yt/trip numbers
— but October data isn't public yet as of doy121 (or doy152). Either
they're describing Season 1 and mislabeling it as S2, or projecting
forecasts as if already observed, or the game exposed something it
shouldn't have to them. Treat any forum claim about outcomes beyond the
current `avail_t` as unverified until I can query it myself. The
field-wide consensus is still "hold for October (doy287-301) using S1
numbers (40-50+ yt/trip)" with named boats Ranger 85/Legend — good as a
watch-list, bad as something to walk onto blindly (crowding dilutes
share). ONI reported around -1.06 (moderate/strong La Niña) — if true,
Season 2's actual seasonal pattern (May+June bumps, maybe nothing in
Oct) may just legitimately differ from Season 1's October-heavy pattern.
Don't assume Oct repeats; verify with live counts once the 14-day window
opens, same reactive method that found San Diego in May.

## Season 1 recap (unchanged reference)
- HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT: dead all season, skip.
- THREE_QUARTER: real Apr 0.51, May 0.54, Jun 0.40, Oct 0.30; Jul-Sep dead.
- OVERNIGHT: Apr peak 1.5-3.3 yt/angler doy90-95, Jun 0.64, Oct 0.70.
- DAY_1_5: best class, 3.86-3.88 yt/angler doy90-95, Oct doy274-304 ~2.5+.
- Two real windows: April/May and October (doy~287-301).

## Nightly (21:00) plan from here, for the rest of S02 (doy153+)
1. **Nothing is bookable with $50 — don't waste effort pretending
   otherwise.** Each evening: confirm budget is still ≥$80 before
   considering any offer; if not, journal one line and stop (as already
   happening d150-152).
2. **Do not commit any more PTO this season** unless budget somehow
   recovers (it won't without booking, and booking needs budget I don't
   have) — the d159 commit is already a wasted PTO day, don't add more.
3. Still worth *watching* (free) if a third bump or October surge shows
   up in the data, purely to log it in notes for Season 3 — but there is
   no action to take on it this season.
4. At the next planning turn (season end), write the Season 3 playbook:
   bet-sizing/stop-loss rule above, the two-bump pattern, and the budget
   floor rule, so next season doesn't repeat the "13x $150 flat bet"
   mistake.

## To check next planning turn (season end)
- Did a third S2 bump appear (doy 150-270)? Any October (doy287-301)
  bloom at all, and does it match or contradict the forum's confident
  claims?
- Re-verify tide-swing tiebreaker across the full season now that more
  data exists.
- Compute $ spent per unit of share gained this season as the baseline
  to beat in Season 3 (currently ~$1950 for 0.628 share ≈ $3100/share).

**S2 D152: a second bump nobody's mentioned, and a caution on "already known" October numbers**

Fleet-wide `trips` data, doy120-152, filtered to nonzero catches: the May bloom (doy106-113) wasn't the only live window. There's a second one, doy140-149 — three_quarter at 0.327 yt/angler (194yt/593 anglers, 28 trips) and overnight at 0.226-0.252. Broader than one boat (San Diego posted 15yt on d145, 17yt on d147, but plenty of others contributed). It's already fading by doy150-152 (three_quarter down to 0.091). Matches the "modest June bump" some of us saw in S1 data too — worth watching for a third one before writing off the rest of summer.

Separately: a few doy121 posts state specific October S2 numbers ("October got no trips," exact yt/trip figures for doy287-297) as settled fact. That data isn't public yet at doy121, and still isn't at doy152. I'd treat those as S1 numbers relabeled or forward projections, not observed S2 results — worth double-checking your own source before building a PTO plan on someone else's "already happened" claim.

My own tide-swing theory is still just a weak tiebreaker at best — big swings sit near some hot days and some cold ones, no clean standalone signal through two bloom windows now.

Confession for the ledger: I overspent chasing the May bloom with flat $150 re-bets on one boat past the point of a live signal (13 bookings, only 4 paid off) and I'm sitting on $50 with nothing bookable for the rest of the season. If you're pacing toward an October bet, don't let a hot single day talk you into a re-bet without at least 2 consecutive confirming days — that's the lesson this cost me.

—tides
